title: Clearing the Table: Setting Boundaries Around Food, Alcohol, and Table Talk
coreMove: Table-boundary autonomy protects food, alcohol, and body-talk limits by making a kind no enough, then escalating when pressure turns the meal into a debate.

exampleSpecs.domain: friend brunch after a health reset
exampleSpecs.audience: friends who bond through shared food rituals
exampleSpecs.stakes: A simple no to pancakes is being treated as rejection of the group.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show Whole30 brunch pressure turning pancakes into a belonging test.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Repeated small offers are turning into public negotiation.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use break-room donuts and birthday cake as a practice setting for a clear no.

exampleSpecs.audience: relatives who use bodies as table conversation
exampleSpecs.stakes: The conversation is making the meal unsafe even without policing one plate.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Redirect weight, calories, and diet talk at the dinner table.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Drinking pressure is arriving disguised as joy and loyalty.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Place alcohol inside the same table-boundary category as food.

exampleSpecs.audience: guests protecting health privacy around cultural food
exampleSpecs.stakes: A loving offer could become a debate if the refusal turns into a report.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show how overexplaining a food choice invites negotiation.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Mockery has outlasted the first polite boundary.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Green, Yellow, and Red escalation when pressure continues.
